_note: THE FEATURE-FLAG PLANE — the pure fold every renderer shares. A flag is delivered three different ways (posthog-ios `PostHogFeatureFlagResult`, posthog-android `FeatureFlagResult`, and the v2 `/flags` HTTP envelope whose payload arrives JSON-ENCODED AS A STRING), and the three must agree on what the app then sees: which flag is ENABLED, what its VALUE is, what its PAYLOAD decodes to, and — the one the SDKs get wrong — the difference between a flag that evaluated false and a flag this project never defined. PostHog's own SDKs answer both with `false`, which is why a mis-typed flag key ships the control arm forever and nobody finds out. The plane resolves it with `known`. Consumers: ClosedSource/DSX/Modules/Core/PostHog `web/index.js` foldFlag (TS/JS lane, executed today) · `swift/PostHogBridge.swift` flagRow (compile-pending) · `kotlin/PostHogBridge.kt` flagRow. Runner note: the closed module facets are not reachable from the open web test suite, so this corpus is executed by the module's own harness; the Kotlin and Swift twins read the same rows.
_note_shape: Each `fold` row is ONE flag as the three lanes receive it. `native` is the SDK result object (payload already decoded); `web` is the v2 `/flags` per-flag envelope (payload a JSON string). `expect` is what BOTH must produce.

fold.name: a boolean flag that is on
a boolean flag that is off
a multivariate flag folds to its variant, and a variant is always enabled
fold._note: The value fold is `variant ?? enabled`, so a served variant reads as the STRING, never as `true`. A renderer that returned true here would make every A/B test a boolean.

fold.name: an object payload decodes on every lane
fold._note: The web envelope carries the payload as a JSON STRING; the native SDKs hand it over decoded. The plane publishes the decoded value, so markup binding the payload never has to know which lane it is on.

fold.name: a scalar payload is a payload
fold._note: PostHog payloads are arbitrary JSON. A lane that assumed an object would drop this one, which is why the action declares `payload` as `any` rather than `object`.

fold.name: a payload the server did not JSON-encode is still the author's value
fold._note: Defensive, and deliberately not an error: a bare string that fails JSON.parse is passed through rather than dropped. Losing an author's payload because it was not quoted is worse than carrying a string.

fold.name: a variant flag can carry a payload too

_note_absence: The three states an unknown flag can be in, and why they are three and not one. `known:false` is a flag the evaluation DOES NOT CONTAIN — the project never defined it, or the key is a typo. `flags_pending` is the evaluation not having arrived yet, which clears itself. Only the first is terminal, and a lane that answers `enabled:false` for either is describing a measurement it never took (X2 typed-absence law).

absence.name: a key the evaluation does not contain is a typed absence
a read before the first evaluation refuses, recoverably
an empty table that HAS loaded is a real answer, not a pending one
absence._note: This is the row `flagsLoaded` exists for: a project with no flags and a project whose flags have not arrived both publish `{}`, and only one of them should make a screen wait.

_note_exposure: `$feature_flag_called` is the event experiments are computed from, so it is emitted on a READ and deduped per (flag, value, session) — an exposure re-counted on every re-render skews the experiment it measures. The native SDKs do this internally behind `sendFeatureFlagEvent`; the web lane does it by hand, which is why the dedupe key is pinned here.

exposure.name: the first read of a flag reports
the same value in the same session does not report again
